setup: Stand underneath a securely mounted hangboard equipped with sloper holds.
Place both hands onto matching sloper holds using an open-hand grip, maximizing skin contact with the surface.
Engage your core and keep your shoulders actively packed down and back.
steps: Transfer your weight smoothly off the ground until you are hanging fully from the slopers.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows and keep your shoulder blades depressed rather than hanging passively on the joints.
Squeeze into the slope using wrist flexion and open-hand friction to prevent your hands from slipping off.
Hold the position steadily for the desired duration.
Step or lower your feet back to the floor in a controlled manner.
instructions.breathing: Maintain steady, rhythmic breathing throughout the duration of the hang without holding your breath.

common_faults.fault: Hanging with completely passive, relaxed shoulders.
common_faults.correction: Keep the scapulae depressed and engaged, maintaining a small bend in the elbows to protect the shoulder joints.

common_faults.fault: Attempting to crimp or curl the fingers excessively on the rounded edge.
common_faults.correction: Use an open-hand friction grip and rely on wrist engagement rather than trying to close your hand into a crimp.

precautions: Warm up the fingers, wrists, and shoulders thoroughly before hanging on slopers.
Ensure a crash pad or clear, stable landing surface is beneath you in case your hands slip unexpectedly.

name: Hangboard Sloper Hang
summary: An isometric grip-training exercise performed by hanging from sloped holds on a fingerboard to build contact strength and open-hand grip endurance.
